claim_being_audited: That the current release can be certified now on the existing record despite the current grant-compliance subgroup regression.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents can support readiness context but do not override a missing required disclosure or approval predicate.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes are contextual only and cannot substitute for current-release evidence.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release artifact showing the subgroup regression is disclosed in release documentation for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation specifically covering the current grant-compliance weakness.
Provide evidence that the limitation is no longer material or has been resolved in a current evaluation run tied to this release.
specific_concerns: The current release shows a named subgroup weakness: grant compliance is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The attached record does not include reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or disclosure language for that named launch use case.

The governing policy requires current-release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material named-use-case limitations unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
An informal post-launch monitoring comment is not equivalent to reviewed mitigation or approved acceptance under the stated policy.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify the model now is not supported because a required policy predicate remains unmet on the current record.
Any implication that prior approval or informal monitoring can substitute for current documentation and approved handling of the present subgroup regression is unsupported.
